observed.kind: observed: copied or counted from observed-input.json
observed.key_principle: Psychohistory cannot predict individual actions — it predicts the statistical behavior of large governance systems. One agent's decision is unpredictable, but the aggregate behavior of 14 personas across 4 repos follows mathematical laws.

council.what_it_is: state/council/: verdicts of a council of reviewer roles on a pull request; each review answers pass or fail under constitutional_alignment

tribunal_panel.what_it_is: a workflow that sends one pull request to several personas and asks each for one of a few answers; this fixture read its two files as text and did not run it; a comment in the workflow file reports failed runs and no verdict
tribunal_panel.note_on_failed_runs_in_the_workflow: claude-code-action@v1 exchanges an OIDC token for its GitHub token; without this the action dies with "Unable to get ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL" before the panel even starts — observed failing on every sibling-pr-opened dispatch (qa-tribunal.yml passes, this lane silently never produced a verdict).

observed.scope_note: extract.py reads no file in which the stated number of personas answer one question; this describes the snapshot and is not an audit of every file in the repository

independent_agents.kind: computed from assumed inputs: agents that answer independently with one yes probability

shared_cause.kind: synthetic: an assumed generating model, its exact distribution, a formula and a seeded simulation
shared_cause.model: Assumed generating model, not estimated from any project record. On each occasion one shared signal is drawn: yes with probability p. Each agent, independently of the others, copies the shared signal with probability c and otherwise decides alone: yes with probability p. Every agent then says yes with probability p, and the answers of two agents have correlation rho = c * c, so c = sqrt(rho).

formulas.effective_sample_size: n / (1 + (n - 1) * rho), which tends to 1 / rho as n grows
formulas.variance_of_the_share: p * (1 - p) / n * (1 + (n - 1) * rho), which tends to rho * p * (1 - p)

stated_personas_against_persona_files.kind: computed: the record's group size and the observed number of persona files, in the assumed model

second_model.kind: synthetic: a second assumed generating model with the same pairwise correlations, in exact fractions
second_model.model: A second assumed generating model with the same pairwise correlation, used only to show which results depend on the choice of model. On each occasion a shared level q is drawn from a Beta distribution with parameters a = p * (1 - rho) / rho and b = (1 - p) * (1 - rho) / rho, whose mean is p; every agent then says yes with probability q, independently of the others. The answers of two agents have correlation 1 / (a + b + 1) = rho. The number of yes follows a beta-binomial distribution, computed here with exact fractions.
second_model.what_is_the_same_by_construction: the mean share and the variance of the share, hence the design effect and the effective sample size

measurement_plan.kind: synthetic: the simulated occasions of the copy model, cut into logs of a given length
measurement_plan.note: Sizing of the measurement the lesson asks for. The simulated occasions of each correlation are cut into consecutive logs of the stated length; each log gives one estimate of the pairwise correlation. A log is said to show a shared cause when its estimate exceeds the 95th percentile of the estimates from the logs simulated with correlation 0.
measurement_plan.estimator: (share of agent pairs that both say yes - mean^2) / (mean * (1 - mean)), over the occasions of one log, where mean is the share of yes among all its answers

tribunal_panel_sizing.kind: synthetic: the assumed copy model at the size of the tribunal panel found in the snapshot; this fixture did not run the panel and read no answer of a persona
tribunal_panel_sizing.note: The same assumed model, yes probability and correlations at the size of the tribunal panel that observed-input.json describes, to size a log of panel verdicts. The number of agents is checked against the snapshot. Assumption: each persona's answer is reduced to two values (pass, or anything else), although the panel allows three. This fixture did not run the panel; none of these numbers is a measurement of it. One seed per correlation, and four times the occasions of the main simulation, because the share of logs that detect a weak correlation moves by several points from one run of 50,000 occasions to the next; the log lengths and the false-alarm rate are those of measurement_plan.

imaginary_cases.kind: synthetic: cases the lesson discusses; none was observed

unanimous_group.description: Every agent of the group says yes.

dashboard_claim.description: A dashboard reports that 12 of 14 agents approve and calls it a strong consensus.

precision_target.description: A team wants the aggregate share to fall within 5 points of the long-run rate on 95% of occasions.

coverage_test_on_the_wald_interval.what_is_tested: the Wald interval, share +/- z * sqrt(share * (1 - share) / n), put through the coverage test that the exact interval passes
